records.claim: Isotretinoin can cause birth defects in 35% or more of infants who are exposed during pregnancy. There is an increased chance of birth defects even if the medication has been taken for a short time. Most of the infants with birth defects will have small or absent ears and hearing and eyesight problems. Other issues that have been reported include heart defects, fluid around the brain, small jaw, small head, cleft palate (opening in the roof of the mouth), and/or missing thymus gland (a gland that makes hormones). Not every pregnancy exposed to isotretinoin will have birth defects. However, it is recommended to avoid any isotretinoin use in pregnancy.
records.source_section: Does taking isotretinoin increase the chance of birth defects?
